exact.Escala común: adelantado, compatible, re: Common scale: ahead, consistent with the scenario, behind, not yet assessable or insufficient evidence. The authors’ assessments are their own words, placed on this scale by the observatory. The observatory’s are fixed or are calculated at each collection with an explicit rule. “Ahead” or “behind” describe the pace against the scenario, not whether that is good or bad.

exact.Líderes calculados entre los modelos del: Leaders calculated among the catalogue models with a score in the {aaIndexName}: those that can be used through the API on OpenRouter and those AA already scores even though they have no public API yet, marked “no public API”. Data from {AA_LINK}, published with its permission. For each model, the reasoning configuration with the highest index is used. Comparable-capability threshold: the best model’s index minus the chosen number of points. Blended price: (3 × input + output) / 4, using the price charged by the lab itself on OpenRouter or, if it does not serve the model, that of the cheapest provider, which is indicated.

exact.Cada barra es el mejor modelo que un lab: Each bar is the best model a lab had released by that date, with the score Epoch gives it today. It only changes when the lab releases a model that beats its record: nothing is interpolated between two records, and the figure is always that of a real model. Colour: the lab’s country; hatching: open weights, both according to Epoch. The thin line is the 90% confidence interval: if two overlap, it cannot be said which one is ahead. The axis starts at {a0} points, not at zero.

exact.Reconstrucción al día con el {aaIndexNam: Up-to-date reconstruction using the {aaIndexName} ({AA_LINK}, published with its permission). The distances are not converted into months.
exact.Hoy y a cada fin de mes, el mejor {aaInd: Today and at each month end, the best {aaIndexName} published up to that date by labs of each country, or by closed-weight and open-weight models, and the difference between them; the top two labs, with each one’s best model. Lab country and weights follow the observatory’s catalogue: a model counts as open if its OpenRouter description presents it as open-weight, even if it cannot yet be downloaded. This is a reconstruction made today, not a series measured at each date: each model is placed at its date according to AA, with today’s index, and only the {n} in the catalogue count (those still on OpenRouter and those AA already scores without a public API), so retired models are missing in the older months.{coverageText} The distances are not converted into months, and the AA and ECI scales are not comparable.
exact.Serie larga mensual con el ECI de Epoch: Long monthly series using Epoch AI’s ECI (CC BY 4.0) and bootstrap intervals; the distances are not converted into months. Source:
exact.Para cada fin de mes, el mejor ECI publi: For each month end, the best ECI published up to that date by organisations of each country (or with closed and open weights, according to Epoch’s classification), and the difference between them. Epoch treats two models less than 1 point apart as having the same capability. Epoch scores models weeks after they come out and does not measure some labs: that is why its figures lag behind those of the AA index. The probability on each card comes from the bootstrap replicates Epoch publishes: it repeats the entire fit by resampling each model’s results, and counts in how many replicates the leader stays ahead.

exact.Escala logarítmica en dólares por millón: Logarithmic scale in US dollars per million tokens (current 3:1 blended price on OpenRouter).
